claim: Mutations in TP53 occur commonly in the majority of human tumors.
source: Mutations in TP53 occur commonly in the majority of human tumors and confer aggressive tumor phenotypes, including metastasis and therapy resistance.
evidence: This is a general statement about TP53 mutations in cancer that is supported by established scientific knowledge and is commonly cited in cancer research literature.

claim: Mutations in TP53 confer aggressive tumor phenotypes, including metastasis and therapy resistance.
source: Mutations in TP53 occur commonly in the majority of human tumors and confer aggressive tumor phenotypes, including metastasis and therapy resistance.
evidence: This statement is supported by established scientific knowledge about the role of TP53 mutations in cancer progression.

claim: CB002 and structural-analogs restore p53 signaling in tumors with mutant-p53.
source: CB002 and structural-analogs restore p53 signaling in tumors with mutant-p53 but we find that unlike other xanthines such as caffeine, pentoxifylline, and theophylline, they do not deregulate the G2 checkpoint.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented throughout the manuscript, including reporter assays, Western blots, and transcriptomic analysis.

claim: CB002 and structural-analogs do not deregulate the G2 checkpoint, unlike other xanthines such as caffeine, pentoxifylline, and theophylline.
source: CB002 and structural-analogs restore p53 signaling in tumors with mutant-p53 but we find that unlike other xanthines such as caffeine, pentoxifylline, and theophylline, they do not deregulate the G2 checkpoint.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5, including Western blots and cell cycle analysis.

claim: Novel CB002-analogs induce pro-apoptotic Noxa protein in an ATF3/4-dependent manner.
source: Novel CB002-analogs induce pro-apoptotic Noxa protein in an ATF3/4-dependent manner, whereas caffeine, pentoxifylline, and theophylline do not.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data showing Noxa induction and knockdown experiments demonstrating ATF3/4 dependence (Figure 1I).

claim: Caffeine, pentoxifylline, and theophylline do not induce pro-apoptotic Noxa protein.
source: Novel CB002-analogs induce pro-apoptotic Noxa protein in an ATF3/4-dependent manner, whereas caffeine, pentoxifylline, and theophylline do not.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data comparing CB002-analogs with other xanthines (Figure 1H).

claim: CB002-analogs target an S-phase checkpoint associated with increased p-RPA/RPA2, p-ATR, decreased Cyclin A, and p-histone H3 expression.
source: By contrast to caffeine, CB002-analogs target an S-phase checkpoint associated with increased p-RPA/RPA2, p-ATR, decreased Cyclin A, p-histone H3 expression, and downregulation of essential proteins in DNA-synthesis and DNA-repair.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data and cell cycle analysis shown in Figure 5.

claim: CB002-analogs cause downregulation of essential proteins in DNA-synthesis and DNA-repair.
source: By contrast to caffeine, CB002-analogs target an S-phase checkpoint associated with increased p-RPA/RPA2, p-ATR, decreased Cyclin A, p-histone H3 expression, and downregulation of essential proteins in DNA-synthesis and DNA-repair.
evidence: This is supported by transcriptomic and proteomic data showing downregulation of genes and proteins involved in DNA replication and repair (Figures 2 and 3).

claim: CB002-analog #4 enhances cell death in patient-derived tumor-organoids.
source: CB002-analog #4 enhances cell death, and decreases Ki-67 in patient-derived tumor-organoids without toxicity to normal human cells.
evidence: This is supported by viability assays and immunofluorescence staining data shown in Figure 6C-D.

claim: CB002-analog #4 decreases Ki-67 in patient-derived tumor-organoids.
source: CB002-analog #4 enhances cell death, and decreases Ki-67 in patient-derived tumor-organoids without toxicity to normal human cells.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence staining data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: CB002-analog #4 shows no toxicity to normal human cells.
source: CB002-analog #4 enhances cell death, and decreases Ki-67 in patient-derived tumor-organoids without toxicity to normal human cells.
evidence: This is supported by sub-G1 analysis in WI38 normal fibroblasts shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Preliminary in vivo studies demonstrate anti-tumor efficacy of CB002-analog #4 in mice.
source: Preliminary in vivo studies demonstrate anti-tumor efficacy in mice.
evidence: This is supported by tumor volume measurements in xenograft studies shown in Figure 6G.

claim: Tumor suppressor p53 responds to cell stress signals from DNA damage, oncogene activation, oxidative stress, and hypoxia.
source: Tumor suppressor p53 responds to cell stress signals from DNA damage, oncogene activation, oxidative stress, and hypoxia. Upon activation by posttranslational modifications and oligomerization, p53 signals cell cycle arrest, apoptosis, or DNA repair, according to the extent of the cellular stress, thereby controlling cell fate and preventing tumorigenesis (Riley et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Riley et al., 2008.

claim: Upon activation by posttranslational modifications and oligomerization, p53 signals cell cycle arrest, apoptosis, or DNA repair.
source: Upon activation by posttranslational modifications and oligomerization, p53 signals cell cycle arrest, apoptosis, or DNA repair, according to the extent of the cellular stress, thereby controlling cell fate and preventing tumorigenesis (Riley et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Riley et al., 2008.

claim: TP53 is the most commonly mutated gene.
source: Thus, it is not surprising that TP53 is the most commonly mutated gene (TCGA, 2020), including in ovarian, colorectal, esophageal, head and neck, lung, and pancreatic cancers that are the most affected sporadic human cancer types (Olivier et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to TCGA, 2020.

claim: TP53 is mutated in ovarian, colorectal, esophageal, head and neck, lung, and pancreatic cancers that are the most affected sporadic human cancer types.
source: Thus, it is not surprising that TP53 is the most commonly mutated gene (TCGA, 2020), including in ovarian, colorectal, esophageal, head and neck, lung, and pancreatic cancers that are the most affected sporadic human cancer types (Olivier et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Olivier et al., 2010.

claim: TP53 is mutated in over 50% of human cancers.
source: TP53 is mutated in over 50% of human cancers and the other 50% involve a biological inactivation of its signaling pathway.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in cancer biology supported by extensive literature.

claim: The other 50% of human cancers involve a biological inactivation of the p53 signaling pathway.
source: TP53 is mutated in over 50% of human cancers and the other 50% involve a biological inactivation of its signaling pathway.
evidence: This is a well-established concept in cancer biology.

claim: Mutated p53 protein results in loss-of-function.
source: Like other tumor suppressors, the mutated p53 protein results in loss-of-function but oligomerization can act in a dominant-negative fashion with regard to the remaining wild-type p53 allele.
evidence: This is established knowledge about tumor suppressor function.

claim: Oligomerization of mutated p53 can act in a dominant-negative fashion with regard to the remaining wild-type p53 allele.
source: Like other tumor suppressors, the mutated p53 protein results in loss-of-function but oligomerization can act in a dominant-negative fashion with regard to the remaining wild-type p53 allele.
evidence: This is established knowledge about p53 function.

claim: Mutant p53 protein can acquire a gain-of-function which contributes to aggressive tumor phenotypes, including enhanced invasion, genomic instability, and therapy resistance.
source: Unlike other tumor suppressors, mutant p53 protein can also acquire a gain-of-function which contributes to aggressive tumor phenotypes, including enhanced invasion, genomic instability, and therapy resistance (Muller and Vousden, 2014; Dittmer et al., 1993; Lang et al., 2004; Xu et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Patients whose tumors carry p53 mutations have a poor prognosis and decreased overall survival.
source: Consequently, patients whose tumors carry p53 mutations have a poor prognosis and decreased overall survival (Wattel et al., 1994).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Wattel et al., 1994.

claim: A common feature of cancer cells is genomic instability due to ineffective cell cycle checkpoint responses.
source: A common feature of cancer cells is genomic instability due to ineffective cell cycle checkpoint responses.
evidence: This is established knowledge in cancer biology.

claim: The majority of cancer cells have an ineffective G1 checkpoint due to p53 mutation but retain a functional G2 checkpoint.
source: Upon DNA damage, the normal cell cycle checkpoint response is to arrest the cell at the G1-phase. In cancer cells, the majority have an ineffective G1 checkpoint due to p53 mutation but retain a functional G2 checkpoint and thus have the ability to undergo cell arrest at the G2-phase.
evidence: This is established knowledge about cell cycle checkpoints in cancer.

claim: Cancer cells depend on bypassing intra-S-phase and G2/M checkpoints for unrestrained cell proliferation.
source: Cancer cells depend on bypassing intra-S-phase and G2/M checkpoints for unrestrained cell proliferation.
evidence: This is established knowledge about cancer cell biology.

claim: Stress signal transduction in the p53 pathway is initiated by activation of kinases ataxia-telangiectasia-mutated (ATM), ataxia telangiectasia and Rad3 (ATR)-related, and downstream checkpoint kinases Chk1/2.
source: Stress signal transduction in the p53 pathway is initiated by activation of kinases ataxia-telangiectasia-mutated (ATM), ataxia telangiectasia and Rad3 (ATR)-related, and downstream checkpoint kinases Chk1/2 that serve as signaling sensors and mediators of p53 activation.
evidence: This is established knowledge about DNA damage response pathways.

claim: It has been a long-standing dogma that ATM/Chk2 and ATR/Chk1 are independently activated.
source: It has been a long-standing dogma that ATM/Chk2 and ATR/Chk1 are independently activated but recent studies provide evidence of cross-talk between the kinases (Brown and Baltimore, 2003; Abraham, 2001; Smith et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Brown and Baltimore, 2003; Abraham, 2001; Smith et al., 2010.

claim: Recent studies provide evidence of cross-talk between ATM/Chk2 and ATR/Chk1 kinases.
source: It has been a long-standing dogma that ATM/Chk2 and ATR/Chk1 are independently activated but recent studies provide evidence of cross-talk between the kinases (Brown and Baltimore, 2003; Abraham, 2001; Smith et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Brown and Baltimore, 2003; Abraham, 2001; Smith et al., 2010.

claim: Chk1 is active in S-phase and G2-phase.
source: Chk1/2 are kinases that participate in cell cycle checkpoint control, with Chk1 being active in S-phase and G2-phase, whereas Chk2 is active throughout the cell cycle (Smith et al., 2010; Zhao and Piwnica-Worms, 2001; Chehab et al., 2000).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Smith et al., 2010; Zhao and Piwnica-Worms, 2001; Chehab et al., 2000.

claim: Chk2 is active throughout the cell cycle.
source: Chk1/2 are kinases that participate in cell cycle checkpoint control, with Chk1 being active in S-phase and G2-phase, whereas Chk2 is active throughout the cell cycle (Smith et al., 2010; Zhao and Piwnica-Worms, 2001; Chehab et al., 2000).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Smith et al., 2010; Zhao and Piwnica-Worms, 2001; Chehab et al., 2000.

claim: Combination of caffeine with irradiation or chemotherapy agents deregulates the G2 checkpoint through ATM/ATR inhibition leading to therapy sensitization and enhanced cell death.
source: For example, combination of caffeine, a xanthine derivative, with irradiation or chemotherapy agents was found to deregulate the G2 checkpoint through ATM/ATR inhibition leading to therapy sensitization and enhanced cell death (Russell et al., 1995; Sarkaria et al., 1999).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Russell et al., 1995; Sarkaria et al., 1999.

claim: Translational cancer therapeutics studies with caffeine were discontinued due to unachievable active concentrations in human plasma.
source: Nonetheless, translational cancer therapeutics studies were discontinued due to unachievable active concentrations in human plasma (Lelo et al., 1986).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Lelo et al., 1986.

claim: There are no FDA-approved drugs that functionally restore the p53 in tumors with mutated p53.
source: Despite efforts to restore the p53-pathway, to date, there are no FDA-approved drugs that functionally restore the p53 in tumors with mutated p53.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of FDA-approved therapies.

claim: CB002 leads to apoptotic cell death mediated by p53 target Noxa.
source: We previously reported a p53-pathway restoring compound CB002 whose mechanism of action was not fully elucidated. We showed that CB002 leads to apoptotic cell death mediated by p53 target Noxa, a pro-apoptotic protein (Hernandez-Borrero et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work (Hernandez-Borrero et al., 2018).

claim: The majority of CB002-analogs tested enhanced p53-reporter activity in a dose-dependent manner within a range of compound concentrations from 0 to 600 μM.
source: The majority of the CB002-analogs tested, with the exception of analog #12, enhanced p53-reporter activity in a dose-dependent manner within a range of compound concentrations from 0 to 600 μM.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: CB002-analog #12 did not enhance p53-reporter activity.
source: The majority of the CB002-analogs tested, with the exception of analog #12, enhanced p53-reporter activity in a dose-dependent manner within a range of compound concentrations from 0 to 600 μM.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Treatment of tumor cells with CB002-analogs at an IC50 concentration (100 μM) resulted in a significant increase in sub-G1 content in SW480 cells.
source: As shown in Figure 1C, the treatment of tumor cells with CB002-analogs at an IC50 concentration (100 μM) resulted in a significant increase in sub-G1 content in SW480 cells.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: CB002-analog #4 increases cleaved-PARP in SW480 tumor cells.
source: Moreover, the most potent CB002-analog #4 was found to increase cleaved-PARP and cytochrome C release from the mitochondria to the cytosol providing further evidence for apoptosis induction in SW480 tumor cells (Figure 1D–E, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: CB002-analog #4 increases cytochrome C release from the mitochondria to the cytosol in SW480 tumor cells.
source: Moreover, the most potent CB002-analog #4 was found to increase cleaved-PARP and cytochrome C release from the mitochondria to the cytosol providing further evidence for apoptosis induction in SW480 tumor cells (Figure 1D–E, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: CB002-analog #4 restores the p53 pathway in SW480 cells independently of p73.
source: As we previously showed for CB002 (19), p53-targets Noxa and DR5 were induced independently of p73 and PARP cleavage occurred despite effective p73 knockdown in CB002-analog #4 treated SW480 tumor cells (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data with p73 knockdown shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Noxa plays a key role in mediating CB002-induced apoptosis.
source: Our previously published CB002 data indicated that Noxa plays a key role in mediating CB002-induced apoptosis (19).
evidence: This statement refers to previously published data.

claim: CB002-analogs induce Noxa expression in DLD-1, SW480, HCT116, and HCT116 p53−/− tumor cells expressing the exogenous R175H p53 mutant.
source: Thus, we sought to determine if CB002-analogs induce Noxa expression in four human colorectal cancer cell lines. In DLD-1 (p53S241F), SW480(p53R273H,P309S), HCT116(p53WT), and HCT116 p53−/− tumor cells expressing the exogenous R175H p53 mutant, Noxa protein expression was found to be induced, though some variation across cell lines was observed (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Only the p53-pathway restoring CB002-analog xanthine compounds and not caffeine, pentoxifylline, and theophylline, induce Noxa protein expression.
source: However, we found that only the p53-pathway restoring CB002-analog xanthine compounds and not caffeine, pentoxifylline, and theophylline, induce Noxa protein expression (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: Knockdown of ATF3/4 upon treatment with 100 μM CB002 or 25 μM CB002-analog #4 abrogated Noxa protein induction.
source: Knockdown of ATF3/4 upon treatment with 100 μM CB002 or 25 μM CB002-analog #4 abrogated Noxa protein induction (Figure 1I).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data with ATF3/4 knockdown shown in Figure 1I.

claim: ATF3/4 play a role in regulating Noxa expression.
source: Hence, our data suggests that ATF3/4 play a role in regulating Noxa expression.
evidence: This is inferred from the knockdown experiments showing that ATF3/4 knockdown abrogates Noxa induction.

claim: A total of 3362 genes met the criteria for significant differentially expressed genes (DEGs) with FDR<0.05.
source: Significant differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were defined by a false discovery rate (FDR)<0.05, and a total of 3362 genes met these criteria (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by transcriptomic analysis data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Out of the 343 genes in the known p53 target gene set, 334 genes were tested in the microarray.
source: Out of the 343 genes in the known p53 target gene set, 334 genes were tested in the microarray but only 197 genes met the low expression cutoff.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the microarray data.

claim: From the 197 genes that met the low expression criteria, 102 genes were found to be differentially expressed.
source: From the 197 genes that met the low expression criteria, 102 genes were found to be differentially expressed (Figure 2A, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is supported by transcriptomic analysis data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Gene ontology (GO) analysis of the 102 DEGs indicated that these genes are highly enriched in the regulation of programmed cell death.
source: Gene ontology (GO) analysis of the 102 DEGs indicated that these genes are highly enriched in the regulation of programmed cell death (Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by GO analysis results shown in Table 1.

claim: Transcription factor analysis revealed E2F transcription factors as having the highest normalized enrichment score.
source: Transcription factor analysis defined by direct binding of predictive binding motifs revealed E2F transcription factors as having the highest normalized enrichment score (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by transcription factor analysis data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Both ATF4 and E2F target genes share common targets with p53 (~5%).
source: The resulting Venn diagram of this comparison shows that both ATF4 and E2F targets genes are not unique to these transcription factors and also share common targets with p53 (~5%).
evidence: This is supported by Venn diagram analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: IPA determined p53 to be activated as an upstream regulator with a z-score value of 3.3 and p-value of 2.9×10−34.
source: Despite p53 not being the top predictive transcription factor in our analysis, ingenuity pathway analysis (IPA) determined p53 to be activated as an upstream regulator with a z-score value of 3.3 and p-value of 2.9×10−34.
evidence: This is based on IPA analysis of the transcriptomic data.

claim: A KEGG analysis for the p53-pathway signaling was obtained with an adjusted p-value equal to 1.18×10−1.
source: A Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) analysis for the p53-pathway signaling was obtained with an adjusted p-value (adjp) equal to 1.18×10−1 that despite not reflecting a significant enrichment of the p53 pathway, it indicates the presence of a total of 31 DEGs out of the 52 genes tested and present in the KEGG analysis.
evidence: This is based on KEGG pathway analysis of the transcriptomic data.

claim: 60% of DEGs are in the KEGG p53-pathway analysis.
source: Thus, this accounts for 60% of DEGs in the KEGG p53-pathway analysis.
evidence: This is calculated from the KEGG analysis showing 31 DEGs out of 52 genes tested.

claim: p53 target genes involved in apoptosis such as Noxa, Puma, and DR5 were upregulated by the analog #4 treatment.
source: In line with the GO terms results, p53 target genes involved in apoptosis such as Noxa, Puma, and DR5 were upregulated by the analog #4 treatment.
evidence: This is supported by transcriptomic data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: KEGG analysis and GO ontology both reflected the downregulation of genes involved in the G1/S-phase of the cell cycle in CB002-analog treated cells.
source: Taken together, KEGG analysis and GO ontology both reflected the downregulation of genes involved in the G1/S-phase of the cell cycle in CB002-analog treated cells.
evidence: This is based on KEGG and GO analysis of the transcriptomic data shown in Figures 2—figure supplements 4-11 and Table 3.

claim: The transcriptomic analysis indicates the downregulation of MCM complexes and origin replication complexes genes.
source: E2F is responsible for the induction of genes in DNA initiation and replication, such as minichromosome maintenance (MCM) complexes and origin replication complexes (Bracken et al., 2004). The transcriptomic analysis indicates the downregulation of these genes and this suggests the inhibition of E2F transcriptional activity.
evidence: This is supported by transcriptomic data and cited knowledge from Bracken et al., 2004.

claim: Downregulation of Cyclin E and Cyclin A genes confirmed the delay of cells to S-phase.
source: In addition, downregulation of Cyclin E and Cyclin A genes further confirmed the delay of cells to S-phase.
evidence: This is inferred from transcriptomic data showing downregulation of these genes.

claim: GADD45, a p53-target gene that can induce cell cycle arrest, was upregulated.
source: GADD45, a p53-target gene that can induce cell cycle arrest, was upregulated.
evidence: This is supported by transcriptomic data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The proteomic pathway analysis of the differentially abundant proteins shows the downregulation of proteins involved in cell cycle regulation.
source: Consistent with the microarray data, the proteomic pathway analysis of the differentially abundant proteins shows the downregulation of proteins involved in cell cycle regulation (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by proteomic pathway analysis data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: CDK4, CKS1B, ERCC6L, MAPK3, and MAX are significantly decreased in analog #4 treatment than in CB002.
source: In particular, CDK4, CKS1B, ERCC6L, MAPK3, and MAX are significantly decreased in analog #4 treatment than in CB002 (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by proteomic data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Out of all significantly upregulated expressed proteins, only four overlapped with the known p53 targets and six proteins with the in-house p53-proteomics.
source: Our results show that out of all significantly upregulated expressed proteins, only four overlapped with the known p53 targets and six proteins with our in-house p53-proteomics (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by Venn diagram analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Eleven proteins were found to be downregulated by analog #4 treatment overlapping with the in-house proteomic database and none with the known p53 target data set.
source: Eleven proteins were found to be downregulated by analog #4 treatment overlapping with the in-house proteomic database and none with the known p53 target data set (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by Venn diagram analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: No upregulated or downregulated proteins were found to overlap in all three data sets: analog #4 treatment and both reference databases.
source: No upregulated or downregulated proteins were found to overlap in all three data sets: analog #4 treatment and both reference databases (Figure 4A–B).
evidence: This is supported by Venn diagram analysis shown in Figure 4A-B.

claim: Differences were observed at the level of protein expression between parental compound CB002 and its analog #4 both downregulated and to a lesser extent, upregulated proteins.
source: Moreover, differences were observed at the level of protein expression between parental compound CB002 and its analog #4 both downregulated and to a lesser extent, upregulated proteins (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by Venn diagram analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Etoposide treatment enhances protein expression of pcdc2(Tyr15) and pcdc25c(Ser16) indicating cell cycle arrest due to DNA damage.
source: As expected, we observed that etoposide treatment enhances protein expression of pcdc2(Tyr15) and pcdc25c(Ser16) indicating cell cycle arrest due to DNA damage.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5A and is consistent with established knowledge about etoposide's mechanism.

claim: The combination of etoposide with caffeine resulted in G2-deregulation as indicated by decreased expression of pcdc2(Tyr15) and pcdc25c(Ser16).
source: The combination of etoposide with caffeine resulted in G2-deregulation as indicated by decreased expression of pcdc2(Tyr15) and pcdc25c(Ser16).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: CB002 or CB002-analog #4 do not increase M-phase marker pH3(Ser10) as would be expected for a G2-deregulator like caffeine.
source: Nonetheless, CB002 or CB002-analog #4 do not increase M-phase marker pH3(Ser10) as would be expected for a G2-deregulator like caffeine (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: CB002 and CB002-analog #4 either do not deregulate the G2 checkpoint or delay cells going into M-phase.
source: This data suggests that CB002 and CB002-analog #4 either do not deregulate the G2 checkpoint or that these compounds delay cells going into M-phase.
evidence: This is inferred from the Western blot data showing lack of pH3 increase.

claim: CB002 and its analogs increase p-Cdc25c and p-Cdc2 in combination with etoposide indicating cell cycle arrest.
source: Moreover, CB002 and its analogs increase p-Cdc25c and p-Cdc2 in combination with etoposide indicating cell cycle arrest.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Cell cycle markers pcdc2(Tyr15) and pcdc25c(Ser16) expression decreased in CB002-analog #4 compared to DMSO and etoposide and their expression over time increased at 12 hr indicative of a delay of cells in the G2 cell cycle phase.
source: As seen in Figure 5D, cell cycle markers pcdc2(Tyr15) and pcdc25c(Ser16) expression decreased in CB002-analog #4 compared to DMSO and etoposide and their expression over time increased at 12 hr indicative of a delay of cells in the G2 cell cycle phase.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot time course data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Cyclin A expression did not decrease over time in CB002-analog #4 treated cells as compared to DMSO and etoposide indicating that cells were delayed in S-phase.
source: Cyclin A expression did not decrease over time in CB002-analog #4 treated cells as compared to DMSO and etoposide indicating that cells were delayed in S-phase.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot time course data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: p-RPA-RPA2(S8) expression upon CB002-analog #4 treatment was increased compared to DMSO indicating replication stress.
source: Moreover, p-RPA-RPA2(S8) expression upon CB002-analog #4 treatment was increased compared to DMSO indicating replication stress.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot time course data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The p53 target p21 was found to increase in CB002-analog #4 treated cells indicating cell cycle arrest.
source: The p53 target p21 was also found to increase in CB002-analog #4 treated cells indicating cell cycle arrest.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot time course data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: CB002 and its structural analogs, unlike caffeine, increase single-strand DNA marker p-RPA-RPA2(S8) and p-ATR(Thr1989), indicating that these compounds result in replication stress and activate features of an S-phase checkpoint.
source: CB002 and its structural analogs, unlike caffeine, increase single-strand DNA marker p-RPA-RPA2(S8) and p-ATR(Thr1989), indicating that these compounds result in replication stress and activate features of an S-phase checkpoint (Figure 5B–C).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5B-C.

claim: PI analysis confirms that combination of caffeine and etoposide deregulates the G2 checkpoint.
source: PI analysis further confirms that combination of caffeine and etoposide deregulates the G2 checkpoint and that CB002-analogs #4 and #10 treatment results in S-phase accumulation are particularly observed at 8 hr following release from synchronization (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is supported by PI flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: CB002-analogs #4 and #10 treatment results in S-phase accumulation particularly observed at 8 hr following release from synchronization.
source: PI analysis further confirms that combination of caffeine and etoposide deregulates the G2 checkpoint and that CB002-analogs #4 and #10 treatment results in S-phase accumulation are particularly observed at 8 hr following release from synchronization (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is supported by PI flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: PI and BrdU co-staining confirm that CB002-analog #4 increases by 30% cells in S-phase at 12 hr as compared to DMSO vehicle control.
source: PI and BrdU co-staining confirm that CB002-analog #4 increases by 30% cells in S-phase at 12 hr as compared to DMSO vehicle control and no significant differences are observed in G2-phase cells between etoposide and CB002-analog #4 at 24 hr (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is supported by PI/BrdU flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: No significant differences are observed in G2-phase cells between etoposide and CB002-analog #4 at 24 hr.
source: PI and BrdU co-staining confirm that CB002-analog #4 increases by 30% cells in S-phase at 12 hr as compared to DMSO vehicle control and no significant differences are observed in G2-phase cells between etoposide and CB002-analog #4 at 24 hr (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is supported by PI/BrdU flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: S-phase delays with CB002 and CB002-analog #10 occur at 6–8 hr of treatment, particularly a twofold difference in combination with etoposide.
source: S-phase delays with CB002 and CB002-analog #10 occur at 6–8 hr of treatment, particularly a twofold difference in combination with etoposide.
evidence: This is supported by PI/BrdU flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The caffeine-treated S-phase population is comparable to the DMSO vehicle control at all time points indicating that caffeine does not perturb the S-phase.
source: The caffeine-treated S-phase population is comparable to the DMSO vehicle control at all time points indicating that caffeine does not perturb the S-phase.
evidence: This is supported by PI/BrdU flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Caffeine decreases the G2-population by 2- to 3-fold at 24 hr in combination with etoposide as compared to etoposide alone.
source: As expected, caffeine decreases the G2-population by 2- to 3-fold at 24 hr in combination with etoposide as compared to etoposide alone, and no other treatment tested decreases the G2-population when combined with etoposide (Figure 5 and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by PI/BrdU flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5 and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: No other treatment tested decreases the G2-population when combined with etoposide.
source: As expected, caffeine decreases the G2-population by 2- to 3-fold at 24 hr in combination with etoposide as compared to etoposide alone, and no other treatment tested decreases the G2-population when combined with etoposide (Figure 5 and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by PI/BrdU flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5 and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: CB002-analog #4 has a 20- to 30-fold range in IC50 values across the HCT116 isogenic panel, independently of the HCT116 p53-status.
source: Across this panel, CB002-analog #4 has a 20- to 30-fold range in IC50 values, independently of the HCT116 p53-status (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by IC50 data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The restoration of the p53-pathway by CB002 or analog #4 is p53-independent.
source: Thus, the results indicate that the restoration of the p53-pathway by CB002 or analog #4 is p53-independent.
evidence: This is inferred from the IC50 data showing similar effects across different p53 statuses.

claim: SW480 cells treated with CB002-analog #4 showed a significant increase of sub-G1 content as compared to vehicle control.
source: SW480 cells treated with CB002-analog #4 showed a significant increase of sub-G1 content as compared to vehicle control, whereas treatment with CB002-analog #4 of normal human WI38 lung fibroblast cells did not significantly increase the sub-G1 cell population indicating that CB002-analog #4 is safe to normal cells in vitro (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by PI flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Treatment with CB002-analog #4 of normal human WI38 lung fibroblast cells did not significantly increase the sub-G1 cell population.
source: SW480 cells treated with CB002-analog #4 showed a significant increase of sub-G1 content as compared to vehicle control, whereas treatment with CB002-analog #4 of normal human WI38 lung fibroblast cells did not significantly increase the sub-G1 cell population indicating that CB002-analog #4 is safe to normal cells in vitro (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by PI flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: CB002-analog #4 enhances cytotoxicity as compared to the CB002 parent compound in the tested colorectal cancer patient-derived organoid.
source: CB002-analog #4 enhances cytotoxicity as compared to the CB002 parent compound in the tested colorectal cancer patient-derived organoid as indicated by the cell viability response curve (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is supported by cell viability data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Immunofluorescence assay staining for ethidium homodimer and calcein shows an increase of ethidium homodimer staining of CB002 and CB002-analog #4 to a larger extent as compared to vehicle control indicating an enhanced killing of cells.
source: Moreover, the immunofluorescence assay staining for ethidium homodimer and calcein shows an increase of ethidium homodimer staining of CB002 and CB002-analog #4 to a larger extent as compared to vehicle control indicating an enhanced killing of cells.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Calcein staining shows that organoids treated with CB002-analog #4 are smaller in size indicating that CB002-analog #4 decreases the growth of the patient-derived organoid.
source: Calcein staining shows that organoids treated with CB002-analog #4 are smaller in size indicating that CB002-analog #4 decreases the growth of the patient-derived organoid (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Cleaved caspase-3 staining indicates that both CB002 and CB002-analog #4 treatment at IC50 doses increases apoptotic cells.
source: Cleaved caspase-3 staining indicates that both CB002 and CB002-analog #4 treatment at IC50 doses increases apoptotic cells (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: CB002-analog #4 treatment results in an inverse relationship with Ki-67 staining with respect to drug concentration, indicating that CB002-analog #4 decreases the population of proliferating cells.
source: CB002-analog #4 treatment also results in an inverse relationship with Ki-67 staining with respect to drug concentration, indicating that CB002-analog #4 decreases the population of proliferating cells (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: CB002-analog #4 is well tolerated as indicated by the mouse body weights during the duration of the experiment.
source: Our data suggests that CB002-analog #4 is well tolerated as indicated by the mouse body weights during the duration of the experiment (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is supported by in vivo body weight data shown in Figure 6F.

claim: At 5 weeks of treatment, CB002-analog #4 treated tumors have a statistically significant lower tumor volume as compared to vehicle control.
source: At 5 weeks of treatment, CB002-analog #4 treated tumors have a statistically significant lower tumor volume as compared to vehicle control (Figure 6G).
evidence: This is supported by in vivo tumor volume data shown in Figure 6G.

claim: Mice xenografted with SW480 shNoxa cells did not have a significant difference in tumor volume after CB002-analog #4 treatment compared to vehicle control treated tumors indicating that Noxa is important for reduced tumor volume in vivo.
source: Mice xenografted with SW480 shNoxa cells did not have a significant difference in tumor volume after CB002-analog #4 treatment compared to vehicle control treated tumors indicating that Noxa is important for reduced tumor volume in vivo (Figure 6H).
evidence: This is supported by in vivo tumor volume data with Noxa knockdown shown in Figure 6H.

claim: CB002-analog #4 is 20–30 times more potent than the CB002 parental compound.
source: CB002-analog #4 is 20–30 times more potent and like the CB002 parental compound restores the p53-pathway and induces apoptosis independently of p73.
evidence: This is inferred from IC50 comparisons shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The 12 p53 pathway restoring structural analogs of CB002 tested were similar in that they resemble the structure of a xanthine.
source: The 12 p53 pathway restoring structural analogs of CB002 tested were similar in that they resemble the structure of a xanthine.
evidence: This is supported by the chemical structures shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Microarray analysis identified approximately 150 genes involved in cell cycle regulation, DNA synthesis, and repair that are significantly decreased compared to DMSO control.
source: Microarray analysis identified approximately 150 genes involved in cell cycle regulation, DNA synthesis, and repair that are significantly decreased compared to DMSO control.
evidence: This is based on transcriptomic analysis data shown in Figure 2—figure supplements 4-11.

claim: Proteomic analysis confirmed a decrease in proteins involved in cell cycle regulation.
source: Proteomic analysis also confirmed a decrease in proteins involved in cell cycle regulation (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by proteomic pathway analysis data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The observed S-phase perturbation may lead to new therapeutic regimens such as synthetic lethality in BRCA-deficient cells and combination with PARP inhibitors.
source: Importantly, the observed S-phase perturbation may lead to new therapeutic regimens such as synthetic lethality in BRCA-deficient cells and combination with PARP inhibitors.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential future applications.

claim: Noxa appears to be critical in vivo as CB002-analog #4 treatment of SW480 shNoxa tumors does not significantly reduce tumor volume as compared to vehicle control.
source: More importantly, we show that Noxa appears to be critical in vivo as CB002-analog #4 treatment of SW480 shNoxa tumors does not significantly reduce tumor volume as compared to vehicle control.
evidence: This is supported by in vivo data shown in Figure 6H.

claim: ATF3/4 can regulate similar targets of that of p53, including p21.
source: ATF3/4 can regulate similar targets of that of p53, including p21.
evidence: This is established knowledge about transcription factor function.

claim: P53 has been shown to indirectly repress many cell cycle genes through the induction of p21.
source: P53 has been shown to indirectly repress many cell cycle genes through the induction of p21. P21, in turn, binds to the DREAM repressor complex which represses genes controlled by E2Fs and CHR transcription factors (Fischer et al., 2016; Engeland, 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Fischer et al., 2016; Engeland, 2018.

claim: P21 binds to the DREAM repressor complex which represses genes controlled by E2Fs and CHR transcription factors.
source: P21, in turn, binds to the DREAM repressor complex which represses genes controlled by E2Fs and CHR transcription factors (Fischer et al., 2016; Engeland, 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Fischer et al., 2016; Engeland, 2018.

claim: CB002 induces p21 expression.
source: We have previously shown that CB002 induces p21 expression (Hernandez-Borrero et al., 2018), as well as analog #4 in this study thus it is possible that the observed S-phase perturbation is through p53-independent p21 stimulation that binds to DREAM complexes.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work (Hernandez-Borrero et al., 2018).

claim: Analog #4 induces p21 expression.
source: We have previously shown that CB002 induces p21 expression (Hernandez-Borrero et al., 2018), as well as analog #4 in this study thus it is possible that the observed S-phase perturbation is through p53-independent p21 stimulation that binds to DREAM complexes.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: It is possible that the observed S-phase perturbation is through p53-independent p21 stimulation that binds to DREAM complexes.
source: We have previously shown that CB002 induces p21 expression (Hernandez-Borrero et al., 2018), as well as analog #4 in this study thus it is possible that the observed S-phase perturbation is through p53-independent p21 stimulation that binds to DREAM complexes.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on inference from the data.

claim: The decrease in tumor volume by CB002-analog #4 is dependent on Noxa.
source: Importantly, the decrease in tumor volume by CB002-analog #4 is dependent on Noxa.
evidence: This is supported by in vivo data with Noxa knockdown shown in Figure 6H.

claim: Noxa is not commonly mutated in human cancer.
source: As Noxa is not commonly mutated in human cancer, its induction by the CB002-analogs offers a feasible therapeutic advantage leading to tumor cell death and its expression may be used as a pharmacodynamic biomarker to predict therapeutic response.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Noxa in cancer.

claim: Noxa induction by the CB002-analogs offers a feasible therapeutic advantage leading to tumor cell death.
source: As Noxa is not commonly mutated in human cancer, its induction by the CB002-analogs offers a feasible therapeutic advantage leading to tumor cell death and its expression may be used as a pharmacodynamic biomarker to predict therapeutic response.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing Noxa-dependent tumor reduction.

claim: Noxa expression may be used as a pharmacodynamic biomarker to predict therapeutic response.
source: As Noxa is not commonly mutated in human cancer, its induction by the CB002-analogs offers a feasible therapeutic advantage leading to tumor cell death and its expression may be used as a pharmacodynamic biomarker to predict therapeutic response.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential clinical application.

claim: CB002-analogs #4 and #10 represent a novel class of anti-tumor agents that provide a unique therapeutic strategy that can be clinically translated.
source: Taken together, our data suggests that CB002-analogs #4 and #10 represent a novel class of anti-tumor agents that provide a unique therapeutic strategy that can be clinically translated.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the collective data presented in the manuscript.
